steps.title: تَ, this time on Form III
body: Form VI's signature is تَ prefixed to Form III's own pattern, giving the shape تَفَاعَلَ — the long alif after the first letter is still there, just with تَ added in front, the same way Form V added تَ to Form II.

تَكَاتَبَ ("to correspond, to write to each other") is a new word built on ك-ت-ب, the same root as كَتَبَ, كِتَاب, and مَكْتَبَة: تَكَاتَبَ الطَّالِبَانِ, "the two students wrote to each other," present tense يَتَكَاتَبُ.

Form VI is most often the reciprocal of Form III — doing the action to or with each other. تَكَاتَبَ is literally the reciprocal of a hypothetical Form III "كَاتَبَ" ("to write to someone"); the shared, back-and-forth action is exactly what the تَ prefix adds.

steps.title: Form VI in one sentence
steps.intro: Read the sentence, then check what marks it as Form VI. Tap 🔊 to hear it.

steps.title: Reciprocal action
steps.prompt: تَكَاتَبَ is Form VI — تَ added to Form III's own pattern. What does Form VI often mean?

options.label: Doing the action to/with each other
Something undergoing an action, with no one performing it
Seeking or considering something to be true

steps.explanation: Form VI's تَ is the reciprocal counterpart of Form III, the same way Form V's تَ is the reflexive counterpart of Form II — تَكَاتَبَ literally means the two sides wrote to each other.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: Which two pieces combine to build تَكَاتَبَ's pattern?

options.label: تَ prefixed to Form III's long-alif pattern (تَفَاعَلَ)
تَ prefixed to Form II's doubled-consonant pattern (تَفَعَّلَ)
اِنْ prefixed, with no تَ at all

steps.explanation: تَكَاتَبَ keeps the long ا of كَاتَبَ (Form III's own shape) and adds تَ in front — Form V instead adds تَ to Form II's doubled consonant.

steps.title: Five forms down
steps.message: Form VI — تَ + Form III's pattern, often reciprocal, the same way Form V is to Form II. Three forms left.
